rubric.item: Deviation: counts outside TableState (no double-count / missed hand)
Deviation: e2e/table.spec.ts BUTTON_NAME gains Hint only

findings.issue: The approved D-2 deviation moved observed counting from the pure nextHand into the session hook (line 207 `observed.current = countObserved(observed.current, done)`) and the snapshot hand-off into `act` (lines 246-248) and Table.onHint (`observedCounts()`). No test exercises any of these lines: SPEC-01/02/03 call countObserved/userObservedSnapshot/applyUserAction directly, the UI acceptance tests pass hand-built counts, and the e2e hint tests never inspect `observed`. Deleting line 207, or dropping the third argument in `act`, or passing `{}` instead of `observedCounts()` in Table.tsx leaves every test green, so SPEC-03's 'acts through the session's act path' and AC#2's 'hint uses the session snapshot' are unverified end to end.
findings.evidence: grep for useTableSession/countObserved/observedCounts in tests/ and e2e/ finds no test that mounts the hook or reads `observed` from a live session; coverage for useTableSession.ts is 28.7% lines in gates/fix-4.json. SPEC-03 test (tests/table/observed-snapshot.test.ts 'decision snapshot equals hint snapshot') builds the snapshot itself and calls applyUserAction, bypassing `act`.
findings.fix: Add one live-session check, e.g. in e2e/hint.spec.ts: an init script that wraps Worker.prototype.postMessage (as delayWorkerReplies wraps Worker) to record payloads; play hand 1 to the end (checkOrCall + runUntilMyTurn), then select Hint at the first decision of hand 2 and assert the recorded `kind:'recommend'` message has `observed` with one entry per bot seat, ascending, each `hands: 1`, and none for the user seat (and, in hand 1, that the recommend payload had `observed: []`). Optionally also assert a stored decision's snapshot via the hand store if records expose it.

findings.issue: `if (decision === null) return;` can never trigger from the UI (the Hint button is disabled unless the bar is enabled, which needs a hand); it exists only to narrow the type.
findings.evidence: TableView renders the toggle with disabled={!bar.enabled}; bar is null when table.hand is null.
findings.fix: Acceptable as type narrowing; optionally replace with `const decision = table.hand as HandState` or leave as is.

summary: All 23 SPEC items are implemented as written, with the approved D-2 deviation. Counting in the hook is correct: it runs inside the existing `reported` handNumber guard alongside the hand-record write, refs survive StrictMode's double effect, holdNextHand/review re-runs are guarded, Deal next / auto-deal / rebuy all go through nextHand after a 'done' step (busted hands are still 'done'), resumed tables start at hand === null so nothing is recounted, and countObserved uses the bot ids from the finished hand so replacements start at 0. act and the hint read the same ref within a decision, so stored and hinted snapshots agree. Hint card copy matches qa.md Q-1 exactly (heading, 'Recommended: ', 'Equity x%'/'Required equity y%', '{name}: {basis}', loading 'Working out the hint…', error line, chart basis and positions); AC#12 templates match Q-2 exactly and explain.test.ts is re-pinned one for one. The e2e/table.spec.ts edit only adds Hint to BUTTON_NAME. e2e/hint.spec.ts and e2e/table.spec.ts pass in Chromium and WebKit (20/20, run by reviewer). One MAJOR: the hook-side wiring that the deviation introduced (counting per completed hand, snapshot into act and into the hint request) has no test that would fail if it were removed.
